mergedParams.userDescription: Thin, elegant text with a very slow, continuous horizontal drift. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

prompts.prompt: Create a minimalist typokinetics preset that treats text like a film title sequence with an ultra-slow horizontal drift. Think of classic cinema title cards - the text should appear thin and refined, floating across the screen like smoke in still air. The animation should be so subtle it's almost imperceptible at first glance, creating a meditative quality. Use a single TextAtom with a continuous translateX effect that moves the text from 5% off-screen right to 5% off-screen left over the entire duration. The text should maintain perfect horizontal alignment throughout the drift, never wavering vertically. Consider this like a long, slow dolly shot in cinematography - smooth, controlled, and purposeful. Add a very subtle opacity pulse (98% to 100%) to create a gentle 'breathing' effect that makes the text feel alive without being distracting.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Single BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' containing one TextAtom. Use className 'absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 whitespace-nowrap' on the TextAtom for perfect centering. Apply font string like 'Helvetica Neue:100:normal' for ultra-thin weight. Create a generic effect with translateX animating from 5 to -105 over full duration with linear easing for perfectly constant motion. Add secondary opacity effect from 0.98 to 1 to 0.98 in a repeating pattern using ease-in-out. Set will-change: transform in containerProps.style for GPU acceleration. Consider using fitDurationTo: 'children' to match text duration. The overflow-hidden on parent ensures clean entry/exit.

prompts.prompt: Design a sophisticated word-by-word typokinetics preset that leverages caption data for staggered horizontal drifting. Imagine each word as a separate layer in your video timeline, with offset start times creating a cascade effect. Each word should drift independently but maintain overall readability. Think of this like multiple tracking shots at different speeds - some words move faster, others slower, creating depth and visual interest. Use the caption metadata to influence drift speed: impactful words drift slower (like they have more 'weight'), while regular words flow normally. The effect should feel like reading text underwater - fluid, dreamlike, with words floating past at different rates. Add a subtle blur-to-focus effect on each word as it reaches the center of the screen, like rack focusing in cinematography.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center overflow-hidden' containing multiple TextAtom components mapped from caption.words array. Each TextAtom gets className 'absolute font-light tracking-widest'. Use word.impact to determine translateX speed: high impact = 80% duration, normal = 60% duration. Create individual effects arrays for each word with translateX from 110 to -110 (viewport percentages), staggered by word.relativeStart. Add blur effect transitioning from 2px to 0px to 2px with peak clarity at 50% progress. Font: 'Inter:200:normal' for consistent thin rendering. Use containerProps.style with perspective: 1000px for subtle 3D depth. Implement using repeatChildrenProps with index-based delay calculations.

prompts.prompt: Build a cinematic typokinetics preset inspired by end credit sequences where text drifts horizontally while subtly scaling. Picture the closing credits of an art-house film - text moving left to right with a very slow zoom that's barely perceptible. The scaling should breathe life into the text without overwhelming the horizontal movement. Think of this as combining a dolly shot with a subtle zoom - the camera (viewer's eye) is both moving and focusing. The text should start at 95% scale and grow to 105% as it crosses the screen, creating a sense of the text approaching and receding. Add a letterSpacing animation that expands and contracts like the text is breathing, synchronized with the drift to create organic movement.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' containing TextAtom with className 'absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center text-white'. Use 'Playfair Display:300:normal' for elegant serif thin font. Create compound effect array: translateX from 50 to -50, scale from 0.95 to 1.05 to 0.95, letterSpacing from 0.1em to 0.3em to 0.1em. All animations use ease-in-out over full duration. Add subtle textShadow effect for depth: '0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.1)' to '0 0 40px rgba(255,255,255,0.2)'. Use transform-style: preserve-3d in containerProps.style. Consider adding very subtle rotate effect (-0.5deg to 0.5deg) for organic imperfection.

prompts.prompt: Create a parallax-inspired typokinetics preset where multiple text layers drift at different speeds horizontally. Think of this like a multiplane camera setup in traditional animation - foreground, midground, and background text layers moving at different rates to create depth. The main caption should be in the middle layer, with decorative text elements (perhaps repeated or faded versions) in other layers. This creates the illusion of depth through motion parallax, like looking out a train window where near objects move faster than distant ones. Each layer should have different opacity and blur values to enhance the depth illusion. The effect should feel like text floating in a three-dimensional space, with the viewer moving through it.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full' containing three nested BaseLayouts for parallax layers. Background layer: className 'absolute inset-0 opacity-20', translateX from 20 to -20. Middle layer: className 'absolute inset-0 z-10', translateX from 40 to -40. Foreground layer: className 'absolute inset-0 z-20 opacity-30', translateX from 80 to -80. Each contains identical TextAtom with 'Futura:200:normal'. Apply blur filters: background 3px, middle 0px, foreground 1px. Use different durations via fitDurationTo for varied speeds. Add perspective: 800px to root container. Consider using sub-preset for each layer with parameterized speed and opacity.

prompts.prompt: Develop a reactive typokinetics preset that responds to audio if available, otherwise defaults to smooth drift. Imagine text that pulses and shifts with music beats like a visualizer, but maintains its elegant horizontal drift as the base movement. When audio is present, the text should 'dance' subtly - think of a handheld camera with slight shake during intense moments. The drift should accelerate slightly during high-energy sections and slow during quiet moments. Without audio, it should perform a zen-like constant drift. The text remains thin and elegant throughout, but gains a subtle glow effect during audio peaks, like stage lights pulsing with the music.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center bg-gradient-to-b from-gray-900 to-black'. TextAtom with className 'text-white font-thin tracking-wider'. Use 'Montserrat:100:normal'. Base effect: translateX from 30 to -30 linear. Add waveform effects if audio exists: translateY with bass response (sensitivity: 0.3, threshold: 0.5), scale with mid response (1.0 to 1.05), textShadow glow with treble. Implement using conditional effects based on audio presence. Add fallback subtle scale oscillation (0.98 to 1.02) when no audio. Use fetcher for audio analysis if needed. Consider internal effect preset 'elegantDrift' for base movement.

prompts.prompt: Design a split-text typokinetics preset where text is divided into upper and lower halves that drift in opposite directions. Think of this like a split-screen effect in video editing where the frame is divided horizontally. The top half of each letter drifts left while the bottom half drifts right, creating a shearing effect that reforms periodically. This creates moments of perfect alignment where the text is fully readable, alternating with abstract moments where the text is artistically fragmented. The effect should feel like looking at text through moving water or heat distortion. Include moments where the halves align perfectly, creating 'beats' of clarity in the animation timeline.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full' containing two TextAtom components with identical text. Top half: className 'absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center' with clip-path: 'inset(0 0 50% 0)'. Bottom half: same positioning with clip-path: 'inset(50% 0 0 0)'. Font: 'Didot:200:normal' for high contrast thin serifs. Top half effect: translateX from 0 to -60 to 0. Bottom half: translateX from 0 to 60 to 0. Both use ease-in-out with synchronized timing for alignment moments at 0%, 50%, and 100%. Add subtle opacity fade (1 to 0.9 to 1) during maximum separation. Use will-change: transform, clip-path for optimization.

prompts.prompt: Create a film-grain inspired typokinetics preset where thin text drifts horizontally with vintage movie texture. Imagine old film stock with text overlaid - the drift should feel slightly unstable, like film running through a projector with minor speed variations. Add subtle flicker effects to simulate vintage projection, with occasional 'jumps' in position like film splice points. The text should have that classic movie title card quality - thin, elegant, but with the organic imperfections of analog media. Include micro-movements that simulate gate weave and film grain texture through very subtle position noise.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full bg-gray-950' with ::before pseudo-element for grain overlay. TextAtom with className 'relative z-10 mix-blend-screen text-gray-100'. Use 'Bodoni Moda:200:italic' for classic film typography. Primary translateX from 25 to -25 with custom easing array to simulate speed variations. Add micro translateY noise (-1px to 1px) with rapid random transitions. Implement opacity flicker: base 0.9 with occasional dips to 0.7. Create 'splice jumps' using step easing at 25% and 75% marks. Add filter: 'contrast(1.1) brightness(0.95)' for vintage look. Consider using internal effect preset for film grain texture animation. Use randomized values within presetExecution for organic feel.

prompts.prompt: Build a perspective-drift typokinetics preset where text appears to drift along a curved path in 3D space. Think of text moving along an invisible arc, like it's painted on the inside of a cylinder that's slowly rotating. The horizontal drift should be combined with subtle perspective transformation that makes the text appear to move away and toward the viewer. As text drifts from right to left, it should also appear to curve slightly, getting larger in the middle and smaller at the edges. This creates a sophisticated carousel effect without being too obvious - maintaining the elegant, thin text aesthetic while adding dimensional interest.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full' with perspective: 600px and perspective-origin: center. TextAtom with className 'absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-y-1/2' and transform-style: preserve-3d. Font: 'Raleway:100:normal' for modern thin sans-serif. Compound transform effect: translateX from 50vw to -50vw, translateZ animating in sine wave pattern from 0 to 100px to 0, rotateY from 15deg to -15deg for subtle turn. Scale from 0.9 to 1.1 to 0.9 synchronized with Z translation. Use cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) for smooth acceleration. Add subtle blur based on Z position for depth of field effect. Consider sub-preset for managing complex 3D transforms.

prompts.prompt: Design a ghost-trail typokinetics preset where drifting text leaves behind fading echoes of itself. Imagine a long exposure photograph of moving text - the main text drifts horizontally while leaving a trail of progressively fading copies behind it. Each ghost should be slightly offset in time and opacity, creating a motion blur effect achieved through layering rather than actual blur. Think of this like onion skinning in traditional animation, where you see previous frames faintly. The effect should feel ethereal and dreamlike, with the thin text becoming even more delicate in its ghost forms.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' containing primary TextAtom plus 4-5 ghost TextAtoms via repeatChildrenProps. Primary: className 'absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center z-10'. Ghosts: decreasing z-index and opacity (0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1). Font: 'Cormorant Garamond:200:normal'. Each ghost has translateX effect delayed by 0.2s increments, creating trail. Primary moves from 40 to -40, each ghost follows same path with staggered timing. Add slight scale reduction for ghosts (0.98, 0.96, 0.94) for depth. Use mix-blend-mode: screen for luminous overlay effect. Consider internal effect preset 'ghostTrail' for reusable trail generation.

prompts.prompt: Create a magnetic-drift typokinetics preset where text appears to be pulled horizontally by an invisible force with varying intensity. Think of this like iron filings being drawn across paper by a magnet underneath - the movement starts slow, accelerates through the middle, then slows again. The text should occasionally 'stick' momentarily before continuing its drift, like it's encountering resistance points. Add subtle rotation wobble during these sticky moments, as if the text is trying to break free. The thin, elegant typography should contrast with these moments of tension, creating visual interest through the interplay of delicate aesthetics and dynamic motion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with className 'relative w-full h-full flex items-center justify-center'. TextAtom with className 'font-extralight tracking-wide'. Use 'Lato:100:normal' for clean thin rendering. Create custom keyframe array for translateX with multiple points: [0:30, 0.3:25, 0.4:20, 0.5:0, 0.6:-20, 0.7:-25, 1:-30] simulating magnetic acceleration and stick points. Add rotate effect oscillating between -2deg and 2deg during stick points (0.3-0.4 and 0.6-0.7 ranges). Include subtle scale pulse (1 to 0.97) at stick points for tension effect. Use spring easing for wobble sections, ease-in-out for smooth sections. Add will-change: transform and backface-visibility: hidden for performance. Consider using helper function for magnetic force calculation.
